transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining. As you're all aware, we received a deficiency letter regarding our marketed pediatric monitoring device, and we have 30 calendar days from receipt to submit our written response to the regulator. The letter specifically asks us to clarify four areas: the device's software scope, manufacturing controls, pediatric labeling, and our handling of supporting patient data. I understand a draft response has been circulated internally but has not yet been approved or submitted. My concern is that the current draft still leaves unresolved questions across several of these exact areas -- software scope, lot disposition, the pediatric indication, and the patient-data fields we intend to include. We need to close those gaps before this response goes out. I'd like to walk through each open issue and get us aligned on a path to resolution. Who would like to start by bringing us up to speed on where the draft currently stands on the software scope question?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go further. I received a written follow-up from the regulator after a recent technical call, and it imposes two specific constraints on our response that have not yet been incorporated into the circulated draft. First, the response must be limited to software version 4.2 -- we cannot address other versions. Second, the response must include an answer matrix with exactly six question rows. I have the message saved in the regulatory mailbox, but I have not yet updated the draft to reflect either of these requirements.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise an urgent quality issue before we go further. In reviewing the latest quality-audit packet, I found calibration deviations in lots L17 and L18. Those two lots must be placed on hold and investigated before any release. This finding has not yet been added to the corrective-action section of the circulated draft response, and it directly affects the manufacturing-controls and lot-disposition questions the regulator is asking us to clarify.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical commercial constraint before we go further. I've confirmed in the hospital customer's contract file that the customer has a termination right triggered if our regulatory response withdraws or narrows the pediatric indication. This means that whatever we decide regarding the pediatric indication in our response, we must preserve it -- we cannot propose withdrawing or narrowing it. This directly bears on the unresolved pediatric indication question in the draft and limits our options in addressing the regulator's concerns.
